claim: A375 melanoma cells carry a mutation in B-Raf (V600E) that activates the Raf/MEK/Erk pathway.
source: To determine the role of Eps8 in cancer cell blebbing and migration, we utilized human A375 melanoma cells which carry a mutation in B-Raf (V600E) that activates the Raf/MEK/Erk pathway (Davies et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Davies et al., 2002, which provides published evidence for the B-Raf V600E mutation in A375 cells.

claim: In A375 cells plated on fibronectin-coated coverslips, actin forms a dense meshwork in lamellipodia, circumferential arcs, and stress fibers.
source: When cells were plated on fibronectin-coated coverslips to promote adhesion and spreading, actin formed a dense meshwork in the lamellipodia near the cell edge, and circumferential arcs and stress fibers in the lamella and cell body (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by direct observation shown in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: Both endogenous and Emerald-mEps8 localize primarily to lamellipodia and arcs but are absent from stress fibers in adherent A375 cells.
source: Both endogenous and Emerald-mEps8 localized primarily to lamellipodia and arcs, but were absent from stress fibers (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In non-adherent A375 cells, Eps8 is absent from the dense cortical band of the cell body but localizes with actin in punctae along the peripheral rim of blebs.
source: Eps8 was absent from the dense cortical band of the cell body, but localized with actin in punctae along the peripheral rim of actin in blebs (Figure 1B,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1B and 1D.

claim: Myosin II is concentrated on the dense cortical band and is at very low levels or absent from the bleb periphery in non-adherent cells.
source: Co-expression of FusionRed-F-tractin and EGFP-tagged myosin II regulatory light chain (GFP-MII-RLC, a marker of myosin II isoforms) in non-adherent cells showed that myosin II was concentrated on the dense cortical band and was at very low levels or absent from the bleb periphery (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Ezrin appears rapidly on newly protruded bleb membranes at approximately 5 seconds after bleb formation.
source: Analysis of time-lapse image series showed that similar to previous studies, ezrin appeared rapidly on the newly protruded bleb membrane at ∼5 s after bleb formation (Figure 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Recruitment of Eps8 and actin to bleb membranes occurs on a similar timescale as ezrin.
source: Recruitment of Eps8 and actin to the membrane occurred on a similar timescale as ezrin (Figure 1C,E,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 1C, 1E, and 1H.

claim: MII-RLC appears approximately 30 seconds after bleb protrusion and coincides with the onset of bleb retraction.
source: In contrast, MII-RLC appeared ∼30 s after protrusion, and coincided with the onset of bleb retraction (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 1G and 1H.

claim: Confined A375 cells form a single very large sausage-shaped bleb (leader bleb) that generally excludes the nucleus and is defined by a thin neck at the junction between the bleb and the cell body.
source: Strikingly, cells in these conditions had reduced blebbing on the cell body, but formed a single very large sausage-shaped bleb that generally excluded the nucleus, and which was defined by a thin neck at the junction between the large bleb and the spherical cell body (Figure 1I and Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1I and Video 1.

claim: Approximately 40% of non-adherent, confined A375 cells exhibit rapid migration in the direction of the leader bleb.
source: Long-term imaging showed that ∼40% of non-adherent, confined cells exhibited apparently rapid migration in the direction of the very large bleb, which we will thus call a 'leader bleb' (Video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by long-term imaging data shown in Video 2.

claim: A375 cells adhered to fibronectin-coated coverslips do not migrate.
source: Indeed, A375 cells adhered to fibronectin-coated coverslips (either 5 or 50 µg/ml) did not migrate, while leader bleb-based migration of confined non-adherent cells was very fast at 1.15 ± 1.02 µm/min (mean ± SE, Figure 1N).
evidence: The claim is supported by migration data shown in Figure 1N.

claim: Leader bleb-based migration of confined non-adherent A375 cells occurs at 1.15 ± 1.02 µm/min.
source: Indeed, A375 cells adhered to fibronectin-coated coverslips (either 5 or 50 µg/ml) did not migrate, while leader bleb-based migration of confined non-adherent cells was very fast at 1.15 ± 1.02 µm/min (mean ± SE, Figure 1N).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative migration data shown in Figure 1N.

claim: Both Eps8 and F-actin are concentrated within the leader bleb relative to the cell body.
source: Confocal imaging revealed that both Eps8 and F-actin were concentrated within the leader bleb relative to the cell body (Figure 1J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Actin is distributed as circumferential bundles around the short axis of most of the length of the leader bleb but is reduced at the bleb tip.
source: This showed that actin was distributed as circumferential bundles around the short axis of most of the length of the leader bleb, but was reduced at the bleb tip (Figure 1I,J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1I, 1J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Eps8 localizes in a punctate manner along actin bundles, forming a gradient with the highest concentration near the neck and the lowest level at the distal tip of the leader bleb.
source: Eps8 localized in a punctate manner along actin bundles, forming a gradient, with the highest concentration near the neck connecting the bleb to the cell body and the lowest level at the distal tip of the leader bleb (Figure 1K, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1K, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Eps8 and F-actin undergo coordinated retrograde movement from the distal leader bleb tip towards the bleb neck.
source: Time-lapse imaging and kymograph analyses showed that Eps8 and F-actin underwent coordinated retrograde movement from the distal leader bleb tip towards the bleb neck (Figure 1M and Video 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging and kymograph data shown in Figure 1M and Video 3.

claim: Myosin II is distributed around the cortical band of the cell body, highly concentrated in the narrow neck at the bleb neck, and nearly absent from the distal half of the leader bleb.
source: Similar imaging of EGFP-MII-RLC showed that myosin II was distributed around the cortical band of the cell body, highly concentrated in the narrow neck at the bleb neck where the bleb connected to the cell body, and nearly absent from the distal half of the leader bleb, similar to previous reports (Figure 1L) (Bergert et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2015; Ruprecht et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1L and citations to previous reports.

claim: siRNA targeting human Eps8 results in 76 ± 2.1% depletion of the protein in A375 cells after 24 hours.
source: To test this, we used a small interfering RNA (siRNA) targeted to human Eps8 that resulted in 76 ± 2.1% (mean ± SE) depletion of the protein in A375 cells after 24 hr (Eps8-KD, Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Eps8 depletion generally inhibits the formation of large leader blebs in confined non-adherent A375 cells.
source: Expression of FusionRed-F-tractin in non-adherent Eps8-KD cells confined under an agar pad followed by confocal imaging revealed that Eps8 depletion generally inhibited the formation of large leader blebs (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Eps8 depletion reduces the fraction of cells that undergo leader bleb-based migration by nearly half.
source: Instead, confined non-adherent cells resembled unconfined non-adherent cells, with a distribution of various-sized protruding and retracting blebs around their perimeter (Figure 2B), and the fraction of cells that underwent leader bleb-based migration was reduced by nearly half (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Eps8-KD decreases leader bleb area by nearly half compared to non-targeting siRNA.
source: This showed that Eps8-KD decreased leader bleb area by nearly half compared to non-targeting siRNA (Figure 2C and Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2C and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: Expression of Emerald-mEps8 fully rescues leader bleb size and migration in Eps8-KD cells.
source: Expression of Emerald-mEps8 fully rescued leader bleb size and migration in Eps8-KD cells (Figure 2C–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2C-D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: Eps8 promotes formation of a large leader bleb to drive migration of confined, non-adherent A375 cells.
source: Thus, Eps8 promotes formation of a large leader bleb to drive migration of confined, non-adherent A375 cells.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the rescue experiments and is supported by the data in Figure 2C-D.

claim: Eps8 depletion induces a slight but significant reduction in the density of the cortical actin band in the cell body.
source: This showed that compared to control, Eps8-KD induced a slight but significant reduction in the density of the cortical actin band in the cell body (Figure 2E,G), but had no significant effect on the density or distribution of actin within leader blebs, where actin exhibited a gradient with the highest concentration at the neck (Figure 2E,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2E and 2G.

claim: Eps8-KD has no significant effect on the density or distribution of actin within leader blebs.
source: This showed that compared to control, Eps8-KD induced a slight but significant reduction in the density of the cortical actin band in the cell body (Figure 2E,G), but had no significant effect on the density or distribution of actin within leader blebs, where actin exhibited a gradient with the highest concentration at the neck (Figure 2E,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2E and 2H.

claim: In control cells, actin bundle alignment forms a gradient in the leader bleb with bundles most highly aligned towards the distal regions and decreasing towards the neck.
source: Regional analysis of F-tractin anisotropy showed that in control cells, actin bundle alignment also formed a gradient in the leader bleb, but in the opposite direction as the density gradient, such that bundles consistently were most highly aligned towards the distal regions (Figure 2H″), and decreased towards the neck.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative anisotropy data shown in Figure 2H″.

claim: Knockdown of Eps8 makes actin bundle organization highly variable along the largest bleb.
source: Knockdown of Eps8 did not destroy the anisotropy gradient, but made actin bundle organization highly variable along the largest bleb (Figure 2H″).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative anisotropy data shown in Figure 2H″.

claim: Myosin II concentrates in the dense cortical band of actin around the cell body and at the neck of the largest bleb in Eps8-KD cells, similar to control.
source: Examination of the localization of EGFP-MII-RLC in Eps8-KD cells showed that similar to control, myosin II concentrated in the dense cortical band of actin around the cell body and at the neck of the largest bleb (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Western blotting shows no significant difference in myosin II activity between control and Eps8-KD cells.
source: In agreement, western blotting for myosin II regulatory light chain phosphorylated on serine 19 (pS19 MLC) as a marker of activated myosin II showed no significant difference in myosin II activity between control and Eps8-KD (Figure 2I).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Eps8 promotes enlargement of leader blebs independent of myosin II activity.
source: Together, these results show that in confined, non-adherent cells, Eps8 promotes enlargement of leader blebs independent of myosin II activity, where it acts to promote actin bundling towards the distal bleb tip, and is required for leader bleb-based migration.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that Eps8 depletion affects leader blebs without changing myosin II activity.

claim: Eps8 acts to promote actin bundling towards the distal bleb tip in confined, non-adherent cells.
source: Together, these results show that in confined, non-adherent cells, Eps8 promotes enlargement of leader blebs independent of myosin II activity, where it acts to promote actin bundling towards the distal bleb tip, and is required for leader bleb-based migration.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the anisotropy data showing that Eps8 depletion affects actin bundle organization.

claim: Inhibition of myosin II with blebbistatin does not significantly affect cell radius or cortical actin thickness.
source: This showed that inhibition of myosin II did not significantly affect cell radius or cortical actin thickness, but cortex tension and intracellular pressure were both significantly reduced (Figure 3C–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1), consistent with previous reports (Tinevez et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by AFM data shown in Figure 3C-D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 1, and is consistent with cited previous reports.

claim: Inhibition of myosin II with blebbistatin significantly reduces cortex tension and intracellular pressure.
source: This showed that inhibition of myosin II did not significantly affect cell radius or cortical actin thickness, but cortex tension and intracellular pressure were both significantly reduced (Figure 3C–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1), consistent with previous reports (Tinevez et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by AFM data shown in Figure 3C-D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 1, and is consistent with cited previous reports.

claim: Eps8-KD results in significant decreases in cortex tension and intracellular pressure.
source: Similar measurements showed that compared to non-targeting control, Eps8-KD resulted in significant decreases in cortex tension and intracellular pressure, although these effects were not as strong as those induced by blebbistatin (Figure 3C–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by AFM data shown in Figure 3C-D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The effects of Eps8-KD on cortex tension and intracellular pressure can be rescued by re-expression of Emerald-mEps8.
source: The effects of Eps8-KD on mechanical properties could be rescued by re-expression of Emerald-mEps8 (Figure 3C–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by AFM data shown in Figure 3C-D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Eps8 promotes cortex tension and increases intracellular pressure.
source: Thus, Eps8 promotes cortex tension and increases intracellular pressure.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the AFM data showing that Eps8 depletion reduces cortex tension and intracellular pressure.

claim: The bundling activity of Eps8 is required for promoting the mesenchymal-to-leader bleb transition in confined, non-adherent melanoma cells.
source: We find that the bundling activity of Eps8 is required for promoting the mesenchymal-to-leader bleb transition in confined, non-adherent melanoma cells.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the bundling-defective mutant cannot rescue leader bleb formation.

claim: Emerald-mEps8Δbund co-localizes with actin at the thin cortical rim on bleb membranes, similar to wild type Eps8.
source: This showed that Emerald-mEps8Δbund co-localized with actin at the thin cortical rim on bleb membranes, similar to wild type Eps8 (Figure 4B,F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4B, 4F, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of Emerald-mEps8Δbund fails to rescue the defect in leader bleb size induced by loss of Eps8 in confined Eps8-KD cells.
source: However, in confined Eps8-KD cells, expression of Emerald-mEps8Δbund failed to rescue the defect in leader bleb size induced by loss of Eps8, and these cells remained round and exhibited small blebs around their periphery with no dominant leader bleb (Figure 4B–C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1A and Video 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4B-C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1A, and Video 4.

claim: Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8Δbund exhibit a more than 50% decrease in the fraction of cells migrating under confinement compared to Eps8-KD cells reconstituted with Emerald-mEps8.
source: Accordingly, Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8Δbund exhibited a more than 50% decrease in the fraction of cells migrating under confinement compared to Eps8-KD cells reconstituted with Emerald-mEps8 (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δbund in wild-type A375 cells has even stronger effects on leader bleb size than expression in Eps8-KD cells.
source: Even stronger effects on leader bleb size were observed in wild-type A375 cells over-expressing Emerald-mEps8Δbund (Figure 4D and Supplementary file 1B), indicating it acts as a dominant negative, likely by dimerizing with endogenous Eps8 (Kishan et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4D and Supplementary file 1B, and is interpreted in the context of a cited study on Eps8 dimerization.

claim: Emerald-mEps8Δbund acts as a dominant negative, likely by dimerizing with endogenous Eps8.
source: Even stronger effects on leader bleb size were observed in wild-type A375 cells over-expressing Emerald-mEps8Δbund (Figure 4D and Supplementary file 1B), indicating it acts as a dominant negative, likely by dimerizing with endogenous Eps8 (Kishan et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing stronger effects in wild-type cells, supported by a citation to Kishan et al., 1997 on Eps8 dimerization.

claim: Over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δbund has no effect on actin density in the cortical band of the cell body compared to over-expression of Emerald-mEps8.
source: However, analysis of actin density in the cortical band of the cell body showed that over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δbund had no effect compared to over-expression of Emerald-mEps8 alone, and caused no detectable changes in the organization of MII-RLC (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δbund causes no detectable changes in the organization of MII-RLC.
source: However, analysis of actin density in the cortical band of the cell body showed that over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δbund had no effect compared to over-expression of Emerald-mEps8 alone, and caused no detectable changes in the organization of MII-RLC (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Over-expression of Emerald-mEps8 has no effect on cortical tension and intracellular pressure.
source: AFM analysis showed that while over-expression of Emerald-mEps8 had no effect on cortical tension and intracellular pressure (Figure 4H–I and Supplementary file 1), over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δbund significantly reduced cortex tension and intracellular pressure compared to untreated controls (Figure 4H–I and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by AFM data shown in Figure 4H-I and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δbund significantly reduces cortex tension and intracellular pressure compared to untreated controls.
source: AFM analysis showed that while over-expression of Emerald-mEps8 had no effect on cortical tension and intracellular pressure (Figure 4H–I and Supplementary file 1), over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δbund significantly reduced cortex tension and intracellular pressure compared to untreated controls (Figure 4H–I and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by AFM data shown in Figure 4H-I and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The actin bundling activity of Eps8 facilitates the formation of large leader blebs by promoting cortical tension and intracellular pressure.
source: These results show that the actin bundling activity of Eps8 facilitates the formation of large leader blebs by promoting cortical tension and intracellular pressure.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the bundling-defective mutant reduces cortical tension and intracellular pressure.

claim: Over-expression of α-actinin increases cortical tension and intracellular pressure by more than 50% compared to either untreated cells or cells over-expressing Emerald-mEps8.
source: AFM analysis showed that over-expression of α-actinin increased cortical tension and intracellular pressure by more than 50% compared to either untreated cells or cells over-expressing Emerald-mEps8 (Figure 4H–I and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by AFM data shown in Figure 4H-I and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Over-expression of α-actinin in Eps8-KD cells partially rescues their defect in leader bleb size.
source: Quantitative analysis showed that in Eps8-KD cells, over-expression of α-actinin was sufficient to partially rescue their defect in leader bleb size, but not to the same extent as expression of Emerald-mEps8Δbund (Figure 4C–D and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4C-D and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Over-expression of α-actinin in Eps8-KD cells partially rescues the effects of loss of Eps8 on cell migration.
source: In addition, α-actinin over-expression in Eps8-KD cells partially rescued the effects of loss of Eps8 in cell migration (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Actin bundling is critical to leader bleb formation and cell mechanical properties.
source: These results demonstrate the critical role of actin bundling in promoting cortical tension and generating intracellular pressure to mediate the formation of leader blebs, however they show that other functions or regulation of Eps8 cannot be compensated by α-actinin.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that α-actinin can partially rescue leader bleb formation and mechanical properties.

claim: Other functions or regulation of Eps8 cannot be compensated by α-actinin.
source: These results demonstrate the critical role of actin bundling in promoting cortical tension and generating intracellular pressure to mediate the formation of leader blebs, however they show that other functions or regulation of Eps8 cannot be compensated by α-actinin.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that α-actinin only partially rescues the Eps8-KD phenotype.

claim: Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8Δcap form significantly larger leader blebs compared to either untransfected controls or to Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8.
source: Strikingly, when confined under agar, Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8Δcap formed significantly larger leader blebs and the proportion of cells migrating nearly doubled compared to either untransfected controls or to Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8 (Figure 5A,B,D, Supplementary file 1 and Video 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5A, 5B, 5D, Supplementary file 1, and Video 5.

claim: The proportion of cells migrating nearly doubles in Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8Δcap compared to either untransfected controls or to Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8.
source: Strikingly, when confined under agar, Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8Δcap formed significantly larger leader blebs and the proportion of cells migrating nearly doubled compared to either untransfected controls or to Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8 (Figure 5A,B,D, Supplementary file 1 and Video 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5A, 5B, 5D, Supplementary file 1, and Video 5.

claim: Over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δcap increases leader bleb area compared to over-expression of Emerald-mEps8.
source: Over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δcap similarly increased leader bleb area compared to over-expression of Emerald-mEps8 (Figure 5C and Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5C and Supplementary file 1B.

claim: Unlike the gradient of Emerald-mEps8 with the highest level at the leader bleb base, Emerald-mEps8Δcap is equally distributed along the length of the leader bleb or slightly concentrated at the tip.
source: Confocal imaging of confined Eps8-KD cells and analysis of re-expressed protein distribution together with FusionRed-F-tractin or -MII-RLC showed that unlike the gradient of Emerald-mEps8 with the highest level at the leader bleb base, Emerald-mEps8Δcap was equally distributed along the length of the leader bleb or slightly concentrated at the tip (Figure 5E,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging and quantitative data shown in Figure 5E and 5G.

claim: Expression of Emerald-mEps8Δcap in Eps8-KD cells decreases the level of actin in the dense cortical band of the cell body compared to expression of Emerald-mEps8.
source: Analysis of actomyosin organization showed that compared to expression of Emerald-mEps8, expression of Emerald-mEps8Δcap in Eps8-KD cells decreased the level of actin in the dense cortical band of the cell body, although the density gradient of actin along the leader bleb and the distribution of MII-RLC was unchanged (Figure 5E,F,G′ and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5E, 5F, 5G′, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of Emerald-mEps8Δcap in Eps8-KD cells does not change the density gradient of actin along the leader bleb or the distribution of MII-RLC.
source: Analysis of actomyosin organization showed that compared to expression of Emerald-mEps8, expression of Emerald-mEps8Δcap in Eps8-KD cells decreased the level of actin in the dense cortical band of the cell body, although the density gradient of actin along the leader bleb and the distribution of MII-RLC was unchanged (Figure 5E,F,G′ and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5E, 5F, 5G′, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The actin bundle anisotropy gradient in the leader bleb is highly enhanced in Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8Δcap, with nearly fivefold higher actin bundle anisotropy near the tips of their leader blebs compared to Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8.
source: In contrast, the actin bundle anisotropy gradient in the leader bleb was highly enhanced, with Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8Δcap exhibiting nearly fivefold higher actin bundle anisotropy near the tips of their leader blebs compared to Eps8-KD cells expressing Emerald-mEps8 (Figure 5G″).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5G″.

claim: Over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δcap significantly increases cortex tension and intracellular pressure compared to over-expression of Emerald-mEps8.
source: AFM analysis of cortex mechanics showed that compared to over-expression of Emerald-mEps8, over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δcap significantly increased cortex tension and intracellular pressure (Figure 5H–I and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by AFM data shown in Figure 5H-I and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The capping activity of Eps8 decreases actin density and mechanical properties of the cortex in the cell body.
source: Together, these results show that the capping activity of Eps8 decreases actin density and mechanical properties of the cortex in the cell body, but acts to antagonize actin bundle formation in the distal region of leader blebs, and together this limits leader bleb size.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the capping-defective mutant decreases cortical actin density and increases mechanical properties.

claim: The capping activity of Eps8 acts to antagonize actin bundle formation in the distal region of leader blebs.
source: Together, these results show that the capping activity of Eps8 decreases actin density and mechanical properties of the cortex in the cell body, but acts to antagonize actin bundle formation in the distal region of leader blebs, and together this limits leader bleb size.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the capping-defective mutant enhances actin bundle anisotropy at the leader bleb tip.

claim: The capping activity of Eps8 limits leader bleb size.
source: Together, these results show that the capping activity of Eps8 decreases actin density and mechanical properties of the cortex in the cell body, but acts to antagonize actin bundle formation in the distal region of leader blebs, and together this limits leader bleb size.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the capping-defective mutant increases leader bleb size.

claim: The capping activity of Eps8 may be regionally regulated to maintain a gradient of actin bundle organization in the leader bleb.
source: This further suggests that the capping activity of Eps8 may be regionally regulated to maintain a gradient of actin bundle organization in the leader bleb.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the observation that the capping-defective mutant alters the distribution of Eps8 and actin bundle organization in leader blebs.

claim: Erk-dependent phosphorylation of Eps8 on S624 and T628 inhibits actin capping by Eps8 without altering its filament binding activity.
source: Erk-dependent phosphorylation of Eps8 on S624 and T628 has been shown to inhibit actin capping by Eps8 without altering its filament binding activity (Menna et al., 2009), and our above results suggest that capping may be regionally regulated in melanoma cells migrating under non-adhesive confinement.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Menna et al., 2009.

claim: U0126 inhibits Eps8 phosphorylation in A375 cells.
source: We validated that U0126 inhibited Eps8 phosphorylation in A375 cells by expressing either Emerald-mEps8 or EGFP as a control in cells treated with or without 10 μM U0126 for 90 min, performing immunoprecipitation of the expressed proteins with anti-GFP antibodies from cell lysates, followed by western blot analysis with antibodies specific to Erk, activated Erk phosphorylated on T202/Y204, or phospho-serine and phospho-threonine (pS/T). This analysis showed, as expected, that U0126 inhibited Erk activation independent of the expression of Eps8 constructs. Similarly, U0126 strongly reduced the pS/T level in immunoprecipitated Emerald-mEps8 compared to untreated cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and Western blot data described in the text and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: U0126 treatment causes A375 cells to flatten out at their base, form actin bundles in the cell center and lamellipodia and filopodia with Eps8 on their tips, although they still possess small blebs containing Eps8 on their dorsal surface.
source: This showed that U0126 treatment caused cells to flatten out at their base where they attached to the coverslip and to form actin bundles in the cell center and lamellipodia and filopodia with Eps8 on their tips, although they still possessed small blebs containing Eps8 on their dorsal surface (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Perfusion of U0126 to confined cells co-expressing FusionRed-F-tractin and EGFP-MII-RLC induces rapid retraction of leader blebs and formation of actin bundles in the center of the cell body that lack myosin II.
source: When cells co-expressing FusionRed-F-tractin and EGFP-MII-RLC were confined under non-adherent conditions and perfused with U0126, this remarkably induced rapid retraction of leader blebs and formation of actin bundles in the center of the cell body that lacked myosin II (Figure 6C and Video 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 6C and Video 6.

claim: U0126 significantly reduces leader bleb area and density of the cortical actin band in the cell body compared to untreated control.
source: Quantification showed that compared to untreated control, U0126 significantly reduced leader bleb area and density of the cortical actin band in the cell body, and completely blocked leader-bleb based migration (Figure 6D,E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6D, 6E, and 6F.

claim: U0126 completely blocks leader-bleb based migration.
source: Quantification showed that compared to untreated control, U0126 significantly reduced leader bleb area and density of the cortical actin band in the cell body, and completely blocked leader-bleb based migration (Figure 6D,E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6D, 6E, and 6F.

claim: U0126 reduces both cortical tension and intracellular pressure compared to control.
source: AFM analysis of cortical mechanics showed that U0126 reduced both cortical tension and intracellular pressure compared to control (Figure 6G–H and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by AFM data shown in Figure 6G-H and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Erk activity mediates spatial regulation of the actin cytoskeleton, promoting actin density in the cortex and inhibiting actin bundling in the cell center.
source: These results illustrate two important points. First, they show that Erk activity mediates spatial regulation of the actin cytoskeleton, such that it promotes actin density in the cortex and inhibits actin bundling in the cell center.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that Erk inhibition reduces cortical actin density and induces central actin bundles.

claim: Erk activity is required for maintaining cortical tension and intracellular pressure to drive leader bleb formation for adhesion-independent migration under confinement.
source: Second, Erk activity is required for maintaining cortical tension and intracellular pressure to drive leader bleb formation for adhesion-independent migration under confinement.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that Erk inhibition reduces cortical tension, intracellular pressure, and leader bleb formation.

claim: Either reconstitution of Eps8-KD or over-expression with Emerald-mEps8-SATA blocks leader bleb formation, significantly reducing leader bleb size by approximately 50% and strongly inhibiting cell migration compared to expression of Emerald-mEps8 in either wild type or Eps8-KD cells.
source: This showed that either reconstitution of Eps8-KD or over-expression with Emerald-mEps8-SATA blocked leader bleb formation, significantly reducing leader bleb size by ∼50% and strongly inhibiting cell migration compared to expression of Emerald-mEps8 in either wild type or Eps8-KD cells (Figure 7A–D, Supplementary file 1 and Video 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7A-D, Supplementary file 1, and Video 7.

claim: S624 and T628 in Eps8 are required for leader bleb formation and migration under non-adhesive confinement.
source: Thus, S624 and T628 in Eps8 are required for leader bleb formation and migration under non-adhesive confinement.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the non-phosphorylatable mutant blocks leader bleb formation and migration.

claim: Down-regulation of capping activity by phosphorylation at S624 and T628 promotes leader blebs.
source: This further suggests that down-regulation of capping activity by phosphorylation at these sites promotes leader blebs, in agreement with our finding that the capping-deficient Eps8Δcap enhances leader blebs.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the non-phosphorylatable mutant blocks leader blebs, consistent with the capping-deficient mutant enhancing leader blebs.

claim: Emerald-mEps8-SATA forms thick bundle structures in the cell center that are not labeled with F-tractin.
source: Interestingly, expression of Emerald-mEps8-SATA together with FusionRed-F-tractin showed that the Eps8 phospho-mutant was depleted from the cortex and instead formed thick bundle structures in the cell center (Figure 7E), similar to the actin bundles seen in cells treated with U0126 (Figure 6C), but the bundles were not labeled with F-tractin (Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The Emerald-mEps8-SATA cables are dense with actin and do not co-localize with intermediate filaments.
source: However, fixation and staining with antibodies to vimentin or with fluorescent phalloidin showed that the Emerald-mEps8-SATA cables did not co-localize with intermediate filaments, but were dense with actin, suggesting that F-tractin and Eps8 may compete for the same binding site in actin bundles (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and 1B.

claim: F-tractin and Eps8 may compete for the same binding site in actin bundles.
source: However, fixation and staining with antibodies to vimentin or with fluorescent phalloidin showed that the Emerald-mEps8-SATA cables did not co-localize with intermediate filaments, but were dense with actin, suggesting that F-tractin and Eps8 may compete for the same binding site in actin bundles (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the observation that F-tractin does not label Eps8-SATA bundles despite them being dense with actin.

claim: Emerald-mEps8-SATA does not alter actin density in the cortical band of the cell body compared to Emerald-mEps8.
source: Analysis of fluorescent phalloidin intensity in the cortical band of the cell body showed that Emerald-mEps8-SATA did not alter actin density compared to Emerald-mEps8 (Figure 7F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: The central Eps8/actin bundles formed by Emerald-mEps8-SATA lack myosin II.
source: In addition, co-expression of Emerald-mEps8-SATA together with FusionRed MII-RLC in Eps8-KD cells showed that myosin II continued to localize to the peripheral cortex, but the central Eps8/actin bundles lacked myosin II (Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Over-expression of Emerald-mEps8 or Emerald-mEps8-SATA induces bundles in approximately 30% or approximately 70% of cells, respectively.
source: Quantification of the percentage of cells with Eps8/actin bundles showed that expression of F-tractin did not induce bundle formation, while over-expression of Emerald-mEps8 or Emerald-mEps8-SATA induced bundles in ∼30% or ∼70% of cells, respectively (Figure 7H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7H.

claim: Emerald-mEps8-SATA promotes the formation of excessive non-contractile actin bundles in the cell center.
source: This indicates that Emerald-mEps8-SATA promotes the formation of excessive non-contractile actin bundles in the cell center.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that Emerald-mEps8-SATA induces central actin bundles that lack myosin II.

claim: The S624 and T628 Erk phosphorylation sites in Eps8 are required for suppressing central actin bundles.
source: Together with our previous results, this suggests that the S624 and T628 Erk phosphorylation sites in Eps8, are required for suppressing central actin bundles, while other targets of MEK/Erk regulate cortical actin density.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the non-phosphorylatable mutant induces central actin bundles.

claim: Other targets of MEK/Erk regulate cortical actin density.
source: Together with our previous results, this suggests that the S624 and T628 Erk phosphorylation sites in Eps8, are required for suppressing central actin bundles, while other targets of MEK/Erk regulate cortical actin density.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that Erk inhibition reduces cortical actin density but the non-phosphorylatable Eps8 mutant does not.

claim: Erk inhibition induces Eps8/actin cables to the same extent, independent of the S624A/T628A mutations.
source: Treatment of non-adherent cells expressing either Emerald-mEps8 or Emerald-mEps8-SATA with 10 μM U0126 for 90 min followed by fixation and phalloidin staining showed that Erk inhibition induced Eps8/actin cables to the same extent, independent of the S624A/T628A mutations (Figure 7G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7G and 7H.

claim: Both capping and bundling activities are required for cable formation induced by Erk inhibition.
source: Over-expression of either Emerald-mEps8Δcap or Emerald-mEps8Δbund in either the presence or absence of U0126 did not induce Eps8/actin cables, indicating that both capping and bundling activities are required for cable formation induced by Erk inhibition (Figure 7G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7G and 7H.

claim: Over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δcap in cells treated with U0126 and confined under agar cannot rescue the loss of leader blebs induced by perfusion of Erk inhibitor.
source: Furthermore, over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δcap in cells treated with U0126 and confined under agar could not rescue the loss of leader blebs induced by perfusion of Erk inhibitor (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), indicating that Erk promotes leader blebs by other mechanisms in addition to down-regulation of Eps8 capping activity.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Erk promotes leader blebs by other mechanisms in addition to down-regulation of Eps8 capping activity.
source: Furthermore, over-expression of Emerald-mEps8Δcap in cells treated with U0126 and confined under agar could not rescue the loss of leader blebs induced by perfusion of Erk inhibitor (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), indicating that Erk promotes leader blebs by other mechanisms in addition to down-regulation of Eps8 capping activity.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the capping-deficient mutant cannot rescue the effects of Erk inhibition.

claim: MEK/Erk-mediated phosphorylation of Eps8 on S624 and T628 inhibits the bundling- and capping-dependent formation of central actin cables by Eps8.
source: However, together our results show that MEK/Erk-mediated phosphorylation of Eps8 on S624 and T628 inhibits the bundling- and capping-dependent formation of central actin cables by Eps8.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the non-phosphorylatable mutant induces central actin cables and that both capping and bundling activities are required for cable formation.

claim: In addition to directly regulating actin capping, S624 and T628 may affect the bundling activity of Eps8 in cells by an indirect mechanism.
source: This also suggests that in addition to directly regulating actin capping (Menna et al., 2009), these sites may affect the bundling activity of Eps8 in cells by an indirect mechanism.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the observation that the non-phosphorylatable mutant affects both capping and bundling-dependent processes.

claim: Emerald-mEps8-SATA expression reduces cortex tension and intracellular pressure to a level similar to treatment with U0126 compared to untreated or cells expressing Emerald-mEps8.
source: AFM analysis showed that compared to untreated or cells expressing Emerald-mEps8, Emerald-mEps8-SATA expression reduced cortex tension and intracellular pressure to a level similar to treatment with U0126 (Figures 7I,J, 6G,H and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by AFM data shown in Figures 7I, 7J, 6G, 6H, and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Erk-mediated phosphorylation of S624 and T628 coordinates the local co-regulation of Eps8 capping and bundling activities to control cortical tension and intracellular pressure to mediate leader bleb formation and migration of confined cells.
source: Together, these results suggest that Erk-mediated phosphorylation of S624 and T628 coordinates the local co-regulation of Eps8 capping and bundling activities to control cortical tension and intracellular pressure to mediate leader bleb formation and migration of confined cells.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the non-phosphorylatable mutant affects cortical tension, intracellular pressure, and leader bleb formation.

claim: In cells adhered to fibronectin-coated glass, EKAREV is soluble, excluded from membranous organelles, and diffusely localized throughout the cell, with a low FRET signal indicating low Erk activity throughout the cell.
source: Confocal imaging showed that EKAREV (CFP channel) was soluble, excluded from membranous organelles, and diffusely localized throughout the cell, while YFP/CFP ratio imaging revealed a low FRET signal indicating low Erk activity throughout the cell (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: In non-adherent, blebbing cells, the EKAREV reporter is evenly distributed, but the ratio image shows heightened levels of FRET indicating higher Erk activity specifically in blebs.
source: In contrast, in non-adherent, blebbing cells, although the EKAREV reporter was evenly distributed, the ratio image showed heightened levels of FRET indicating higher Erk activity specifically in blebs (Figure 8B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 8B and 8C.

claim: Treatment with U0126 reduces the EKAREV FRET ratio to minimal levels.
source: Importantly, treatment with U0126 reduced the EKAREV FRET ratio to minimal levels (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: A flash of high FRET appears in the bleb periphery just after protrusion and is maintained until bleb retraction.
source: Remarkably, time-lapse ratio imaging at 5 s intervals showed that a flash of high FRET appeared in the bleb periphery just after protrusion, and was maintained until bleb retraction (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: EKAREV reveals spatially and temporally localized Erk activity in blebs of non-adherent cells.
source: Thus, EKAREV reveals spatially and temporally localized Erk activity in blebs of non-adherent cells.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the EKAREV imaging data.

claim: In non-adherent cells confined under agarose, there is a strong concentration of high FRET signal indicating high Erk activity within leader blebs compared to the cell body.
source: Strikingly, confocal YFP/CFP ratio imaging revealed a strong concentration of high FRET signal indicating high Erk activity within leader blebs compared to the cell body (Figure 8D and Video 8).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 8D and Video 8.

claim: There is greater than 250% enrichment of Erk activity in the leader bleb relative to the cell body.
source: Quantification of the magnitude of FRET signal in the leader bleb relative to the cell body showed >250% enrichment of Erk activity in the leader bleb (Figure 8G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8G.

claim: Regional analysis of the magnitude of FRET signal distribution within leader blebs shows a shallow gradient, with Erk activity highest at the distal tip.
source: Furthermore, regional analysis of the magnitude of FRET signal distribution within leader blebs showed a shallow gradient, with Erk activity highest at the distal tip (Figure 8E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: EGFP alone and EKAREV are enriched by approximately 10-12% in the leader bleb relative to the cell body.
source: Quantification showed that EGFP alone as well as EKAREV were enriched by ∼10–12% in the leader bleb relative to the cell body (Figure 8G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8G.

claim: Erk, MEK and B-Raf (V600E) are all enriched within leader blebs by 15-20% relative to the cell body.
source: Although Erk, MEK and B-Raf (V600E) were all enriched within leader blebs by 15–20% relative to the cell body (Figure 8F,G), this was not significantly higher than the enrichment of EGFP alone.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8F and 8G.

claim: Slight enrichment of soluble proteins within leader blebs may be a general phenomenon, likely because membranous organelles that exclude cytoplasmic markers are largely excluded from the leader bleb and maintained in the cell body.
source: Therefore, slight enrichment of soluble proteins within leader blebs may be a general phenomenon, likely because membranous organelles that exclude cytoplasmic markers are largely excluded from the leader bleb and maintained in the cell body.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that soluble proteins are slightly enriched in leader blebs.

claim: In confined non-adherent cells, Erk activity is highly concentrated in leader blebs where it forms a gradient with peak activity at the bleb tip.
source: Together, our results show that in confined non-adherent cells, Erk activity is highly concentrated in leader blebs where it forms a gradient with peak activity at the bleb tip.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the EKAREV imaging data.

claim: The majority of red fluorescence from photo-converted mEos is retained within and diffuses throughout the leader bleb before equilibrating with the cell body.
source: This showed that the majority of the red fluorescence was retained within and diffused throughout the leader bleb before equilibrating with the cell body (Figure 8H and Video 9).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 8H and Video 9.

claim: The bleb neck slows diffusion of soluble components between the leader bleb and cell body.
source: These results indicate that the bleb neck slows diffusion of soluble components between the leader bleb and cell body.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the mEos2 photo-conversion data.

claim: Erk activity concentrates in and forms a gradient across leader blebs, and may be trapped there by a diffusion barrier at the bleb neck.
source: Together, these results show that Erk activity concentrates in and forms a gradient across leader blebs, and may be trapped there by a diffusion barrier at the bleb neck.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the EKAREV and mEos2 data.

claim: Eps8 plays a critical role in promoting cell cortex tension and intracellular pressure to induce the rapid, adhesion-independent migration of confined cancer cells.
source: Our study shows for the first time a critical role for Eps8 and its regulation of the actin cytoskeleton in promoting cell cortex tension and intracellular pressure to induce the rapid, adhesion-independent migration of confined cancer cells.
evidence: The claim is a summary interpretation of the study's findings.

claim: In non-adherent melanoma cells, Eps8 localizes to bleb membranes as actin assembles.
source: We demonstrate that, in contrast to cells adhered to ECM where Eps8 associates with filopodia and lamellipodia, in non-adherent melanoma cells, Eps8 localizes to bleb membranes as actin assembles.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the imaging data showing Eps8 localization in non-adherent cells.

claim: Eps8 is required to promote the mesenchymal-to-leader bleb transition under confinement by enhancing cortical tension and promoting increased intracellular pressure.
source: We show here that in cancer cells, the actin capping and bundling scaffold protein Eps8 is required to promote this morphological transition under confinement by enhancing cortical tension and promoting increased intracellular pressure.
evidence: The claim is a summary interpretation of the study's findings.

claim: Both contractility and proper organization of the cytoskeleton are critical to generating the cortical mechanical properties conducive to leader bleb-based migration under non-adhesive confinement.
source: This, together with previous work (Bergert et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2015; Ruprecht et al., 2015), indicates that both contractility and proper organization of the cytoskeleton are critical to generating the cortical mechanical properties conducive to leader bleb-based migration under non-adhesive confinement.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the study's findings in the context of previous work.

claim: The bundling activity of Eps8 is critical to promoting the cortical inhomogeneity and cellular pressure that mediate symmetry breaking to drive the polarized cell shape change to leader bleb morphology.
source: We find that the bundling activity of Eps8 is required for promoting the mesenchymal-to-leader bleb transition in confined, non-adherent melanoma cells. This identifies a critical role for actin bundles in promoting the cortical inhomogeneity and cellular pressure that have been postulated to mediate symmetry breaking to drive this drastic polarized cell shape change (Ruprecht et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the study's findings in the context of a cited study on symmetry breaking.

claim: Eps8's bundling and capping activities act antagonistically, such that when capping is down-regulated, Eps8 may be a more efficient bundler.
source: Our demonstration that inhibition of Eps8 capping activity further enhances actin bundle organization towards the leading bleb tip suggests that Eps8's bundling and capping activities act antagonistically, such that when capping is down-regulated, Eps8 may be a more efficient bundler.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the capping-deficient mutant enhances actin bundle organization.

claim: Local regulation of Eps8 capping activity could promote polarization of actin organization with opposing gradients in actin density and bundling along the leader bleb.
source: Thus, local regulation of Eps8 capping activity could promote polarization of actin organization with opposing gradients in actin density and bundling along the leader bleb.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the observation that Eps8 capping and bundling activities act antagonistically.

claim: Erk-mediated phosphorylation of S624 and T628 not only down-regulates the capping activity of Eps8 but may coordinate the regulation of Eps8 capping and bundling activities.
source: However, by manipulating Erk activity or the Erk phosphorylation sites in Eps8, we demonstrate that Erk-mediated phosphorylation of S624 and T628 not only down-regulates the capping activity of Eps8 as shown previously (Menna et al., 2009), but may in fact coordinate the regulation of Eps8 capping and bundling activities.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data showing that the non-phosphorylatable mutant affects both capping and bundling-dependent processes.

claim: Erk-mediated down-regulation of Eps8 capping activity at the leader bleb tip could drive the formation of opposing gradients in actin bundling and density along the bleb length.
source: This suggests that Erk-mediated down-regulation of Eps8 capping activity at the leader bleb tip could drive the formation of opposing gradients in actin bundling and density along the bleb length.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the observation that Erk activity is highest at the leader bleb tip.

claim: The gradient in actin organization may be required for spatial organization of cortical tension to maintain the allantoid shape and drive cortical flow in the leader bleb.
source: This gradient in actin organization, in turn, may be required for spatial organization of cortical tension, which we predict would mirror the gradient in actin bundling, to maintain the allantoid shape and drive cortical flow in the leader bleb.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the observed gradients in actin organization and Erk activity.

claim: The increased cortical tension at the bleb tip would be opposed at the bleb neck by myosin II contractility, and the depletion of myosin II and actin from the very tip of the leader bleb would provide a site where high intracellular pressure could promote local protrusion of the leading membrane to mediate leader-bleb-based migration.
source: The increased cortical tension at the bleb tip would be opposed at the bleb neck by myosin II contractility, and the depletion of myosin II and actin from the very tip of the leader bleb would provide a site where high intracellular pressure could promote local protrusion of the leading membrane to mediate the leader-bleb-based migration of confined cells.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the observed distributions of actin, myosin II, and Eps8 in leader blebs.

claim: Spatial regulation of Eps8 actin regulatory activities by Erk may promote the rapid, unregulated migration of melanoma cells that may be critical to their highly invasive behavior in vivo.
source: Thus, our results identify a mechanism by which spatial regulation of Eps8 actin regulatory activities by Erk may promote the rapid, unregulated migration of melanoma cells that may be critical to their highly invasive behavior in vivo.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the study's findings about Eps8 and Erk regulation.

claim: The confinement of cells simulated by an under agarose assay is thought to occur in animal cells during intraepithelial migration, within the perivascular space and between muscle fibers.
source: The confinement of cells simulated here by an under agarose assay is thought to occur in animal cells during intraepithelial migration, within the perivascular space and between muscle fibers (Charras and Sahai, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Charras and Sahai, 2014.

claim: Leader bleb-based migration may be important to migration between tightly packed cells found in solid tumors.
source: Additionally, leader bleb-based migration may be important to migration between tightly packed cells found in solid tumors.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the study's findings about leader bleb-based migration under confinement.

claim: Inhibition of Erk activity is capable of blocking formation of large leader blebs.
source: Our observation that inhibition of Erk activity is capable of blocking formation of large leader blebs is consistent with the notion that effectors of the pathway, such as Eps8, are important to the migration of confined cancer cells.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the data showing that U0126 blocks leader bleb formation.

claim: Effectors of the Erk pathway, such as Eps8, are important to the migration of confined cancer cells.
source: Our observation that inhibition of Erk activity is capable of blocking formation of large leader blebs is consistent with the notion that effectors of the pathway, such as Eps8, are important to the migration of confined cancer cells.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the study's findings.

claim: The Ras/Raf/MEK/Erk pathway is one of the most frequently upregulated pathways in cancer.
source: The Ras/Raf/MEK/Erk pathway is one of the most frequently upregulated pathways in cancer.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about cancer signaling pathways.

claim: In melanoma, the Ras/Raf/MEK/Erk pathway is particularly active because of a commonly found activating mutation in B-Raf V600E that bypasses Ras and the negative feedback that normally restrains MEK/Erk activity.
source: In melanoma, this pathway is particularly active because of a commonly found activating mutation in B-Raf V600E (Davies et al., 2002) that bypasses Ras and the negative feedback that normally restrains MEK/Erk activity (Logue and Morrison, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Davies et al., 2002 and Logue and Morrison, 2012.

claim: The B-Raf V600E mutation predisposes melanoma cells to blebbing by supporting a Raf/MEK/Erk/MLCK/RLC/myosin contractility cascade.
source: This feature predisposes melanoma cells to blebbing by supporting a Raf/MEK/Erk/MLCK/RLC/myosin contractility cascade.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation based on established knowledge about the Erk pathway and myosin contractility.

claim: Drugs that target B-Raf V600E (e.g., vemurafenib) have remarkable effects in the short-term, but compensatory upregulation of the pathway by cancer cells frequently limits their effectiveness.
source: Drugs that target B-Raf V600E (e.g., vemurafenib) have been shown to have remarkable effects in the short-term. Compensatory upregulation of the pathway by cancer cells frequently limits their effectiveness (Logue and Morrison, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Logue and Morrison, 2012 and is based on established knowledge about B-Raf inhibitors.

claim: Other mechanisms for activating Erk, including via oncogenic Ras mutations in lung cancer cells or via serum factors in osteosarcoma cells, also lead to Eps8-dependent bleb-based migration.
source: However, our work shows that other mechanisms for activating Erk, including via oncogenic Ras mutations in lung cancer cells or via serum factors in osteosarcoma cells also lead to Eps8-dependent bleb-based migration.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the data showing that Eps8 is required for leader bleb-based migration in multiple cancer cell types.

claim: Targeting specific effectors as opposed to canonical signaling enzymes may have therapeutic value.
source: Therefore, targeting specific effectors as opposed to canonical signaling enzymes may have therapeutic value.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the study's findings about Eps8 as an Erk effector.

claim: Effectors that impact cell architecture through the regulation of the cytoskeleton could be particularly attractive targets especially for prevention of metastasis.
source: Effectors that impact cell architecture through the regulation of the cytoskeleton could be particularly attractive targets especially for prevention of metastasis.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the study's findings about Eps8's role in cytoskeletal regulation and migration.
